maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a capacity-sweep matrix for embed + rerank for a midweek traffic spike. Repro'd tail behavior where batch jobs start spilling into realtime pools. Need a quick sync on mitigations.

simon: Can you paste the numbers? p95 latency impact, GPU-hr delta?

maya: Short summary: forecasted 2.7x q/q midweek peak for embedding queries (search/rerank). With our current separate pools (embed-batch, rerank-realtime) the batch queueing pressure starts at ~0.8x peak and causes spillover.

maya: Baseline capacity to keep no-spill SLOs: embed-batch ~120 GPU-hrs/day, rerank-realtime ~300 GPU-hrs/day. If we allow controlled spill to shared-lowpri, incremental runtime ~+30 GPU-hrs/day but p95 rerank jumps from ~45ms to ~165ms.

lee: Do we have sims for pre-warm KV/cache and how much latency that saves?

maya: Paste from the sweep run:
```
# capacity-sweep results (sample)
config: separate
peak_mult: 2.7
embed_batch: 120gpu-hrs/day
rerank_realtime: 300gpu-hrs/day
shared_spill_threshold: 0.8
p95_rerank_no_spill: 45ms
p95_rerank_spill: 165ms
```

arjun: If we compress batch windows (move more to off-peak) we can shave hours. Moving ~35% of batch to nightly saves ~40 GPU-hrs/day but that raises embedding freshness/backlog SLA.

simon: Also note: shared-lowpri is in GCP-europe1 with egress caps. Cross-region spill -> extra egress + networking cost (~+18% estimated) and possible throttles.

incident-bot: capacity-sweep job 1912345678 completed; artifacts: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/1912345678

maya: Proposed mitigations (fast):
1) Add 2 reserved nodes to rerank-realtime as a midweek hot-spare (8–20 UTC) -> roughly +24 GPU-hrs/day but keeps p95 low.
2) KV pre-warm + increase batch windowing to move non-urgent slices to off-peak -> save ~30–45 GPU-hrs/day.
3) Enable controlled per-tenant spill to shared-lowpri with per-tenant rate limits and SLA opt-in. This reduces cost but needs throttles and billing flags.

lee: @maya can you open a quick runbook for 1) and assign owners? I can take the KV pre-warm script.

maya: Runbook created (placeholder): https://go/runbooks/eng/1912345678. Owners: lee (KV prewarm), simon (region routing), arjun (batch scheduler). Tagging @oncall for weekend watch.

oncall-bot: oncall: @ops rotation notified.

simon: I agree with 1+2. For 3 we need per-tenant opt-in or hard throttle high-QPS tenants before allowing spill — otherwise multi-tenant risk is too high. Also recommend a short AB test: 10% traffic, single tenant, measure p95/regressions.

maya: I'll schedule a 30m triage in #eng-infra in 20m. If you can't make it, drop notes in the runbook.

arjun: Quick ask — can infra run a cost-sensitivity sim with cross-region spill included (+egress)? That will decide whether we prefer hot-spare vs spill.

maya: Added sim request to the job queue (priority=high).

simon: Thanks — if we greenlight hot-spare, I'll scope infra changes (routing, autoscaler overrides) and a short deploy playbook.

maya: TL;DR — we can avoid dangerous spill with small hot-spare + KV prewarm, net cost ~+10–12% vs potential latency hit and unknown egress costs if we rely on spill. Need decision by EOD for midweek rollout prep.

lee: +1 for 1+2. I'll start KV script and post perf diffs.

maya: Thanks all.
